title: Agent-Based Macroeconomics
publisher: Bielefeld University, Faculty of Business Administration and Economics (Working Papers in Economics and Management No. 02-2018); chapter for Handbook of Computational Economics Vol. IV

key_points.claim: The chapter surveys macroeconomic agent-based models (MABMs), compares their structure and finds an emerging common core across model families.
key_points.evidence_quote: identifying what could be considered an emerging common core of macroeconomic agent-based modeling.

key_points.claim: Agent-based macroeconomics has early roots: Simon (1959) called for models of heterogeneous adaptive agents, and 1970s micro-founded simulations (MOSES, Transactions Model) were early examples.
key_points.evidence_quote: micro founded simulation models of the Swedish economy (the MOSES model, see Eliason (1977, 1984)) and the U.S. economy

key_points.claim: MABMs jointly reproduce empirical stylized facts (time series and fat-tailed distributions) at different aggregation levels, which is hard for alternative approaches.
key_points.evidence_quote: Being able to jointly reproduce empirical stylized facts with respect to time series properties and distributional properties at different levels of aggregation is certainly a very appealing feature of MABMs

key_points.claim: Interaction produces non-linearities and positive feedbacks, giving path dependence and endogenous crashes and crises, which suits policy and institutional design studies.
key_points.evidence_quote: These properties of MABMs are also the basis for endogenously generating extreme events, like crashes and economic crises

key_points.claim: Agent behaviour: no equilibrium or rational expectations is assumed; agents follow bounded-rational heuristics or rules of thumb informed by psychological and empirical or experimental evidence. Lack of a common basis for bounded rationality remains a concern.
key_points.evidence_quote: in agent-based macroeconomic models it is not assumed that the economy is in equilibrium and that individuals have rational expectations

key_points.claim: The main model families compared are EURACE (Unibi and Genoa versions), JAMEL, Keynes meeting Schumpeter (KS), LAGOM and Lengnick's small model.
key_points.evidence_quote: the family of models developed by Dosi, Fagiolo, Roventini and co-authors in Pisa, known as the “Keynes meeting Schumpeter” framework (KS)

reliability_notes: Full text of an 84-page PDF working paper by respected authors (Dawid, Delli Gatti). I read only the abstract, the intro and the model list, not the full policy sections. It covers the economic domain of artificial societies only. It is a 2018 survey, so newer work is missing.
